questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Argument of a Complex Number in the Third Quadrant
questions.problem:
Find, in radians to two decimal places, the argument of $z=-3-4\text{i}.$ 

**Hint**: The argument of a complex number is in the range $[0,2\pi ).$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's plot $z$ in the complex plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13930486/assets/7eff12ed4bca73dc27f834b0740b5b2235440250e11427f911c8fc29c99fa1d7.png)

The complex number $z$ lies in the third quadrant of the complex plane. Therefore $\pi <arg⁡(z)<\frac{3\pi }{2}.$ If $\alpha $ is the angle that $z$ makes with the negative real axis, then

$$
\begin{aligned}\alpha  & =arctan⁡(\frac{4}{3})≈0.927\,30.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =arg⁡(z)≈\pi +0.927\,30≈4.07
$$

to two decimal places.

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Argument of a Complex Number in the Fourth Quadrant
questions.problem:
Find, in radians to two decimal places, the argument of $z=9-6\text{i}.$ 

**Hint**: The argument of a complex number is in the range $[0,2\pi ).$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's plot $z$ in the complex plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13930486/assets/1bc5f38d44d9df32a7493f8d210bbc17d716d8a63316e3d730a1c4258d56fe46.png)

The complex number $z$ lies in the fourth quadrant of the complex plane. Therefore $\frac{3\pi }{2}<arg⁡(z)<2\pi .$ 

If $\alpha $ is the angle that $z$ makes with the positive real axis, then

$$
\alpha =arctan⁡(\frac{6}{9})=arctan⁡(\frac{2}{3})≈0.588\,00.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =arg⁡(z)=2\pi -0.588\,00≈5.70
$$

to two decimal places.

**Hint**: The argument of a complex number is in the range $[0,2\pi ).$ 

$arg⁡(z)≈$

questions.worked_solution:
Let's plot $z$ in the complex plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13930486/assets/d3b5558c0268843618c52c588ffcf1c8012189041b17d52fadd6fe74c3526700.png)

The complex number $z$ lies in the second quadrant of the complex plane. Hence $\frac{\pi }{2}<arg⁡(z)<\pi .$ 

If $\alpha $ is the angle that $z$ makes with the negative real axis, then

$$
\begin{aligned}tan⁡\alpha  & =\frac{8}{11} \\ \alpha  & =arctan⁡(\frac{8}{11}) \\  & =0.628\text{ }796\text{ }…\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =arg⁡(z)=\pi -0.628\text{ }796\text{ }…≈2.51,

rounded to $2$ decimal places.

questions.problem:

**Hint**: The argument of a complex number is in the range $[0,2\pi ).$ 

$arg⁡(z)=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
Let's plot $z$ in the complex plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13930486/assets/f466a110eda3b07b50d988de6e46a541ad85d7ff64f43a6f056ea216752fa2d9.png)

The complex number $z$ lies in the second quadrant of the complex plane. Hence $\frac{\pi }{2}<arg⁡(z)<\pi .$ 

If $\alpha $ is the angle that $z$ makes with the negative real axis, then

$$
\begin{aligned}tan⁡\alpha  & =\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{5} \\ \alpha  & =arctan⁡(\sqrt{3}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =arg⁡(z)=\pi -\frac{\pi }{3}=\frac{2\pi }{3}.
$$
